bib.title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision

question: Can self-supervised learning on a large curated image dataset produce general-purpose frozen visual features that match or beat the best weakly-supervised (text-guided) features at image and pixel level?
hypothesis: Existing SSL methods, trained on enough curated and diverse data at scale, can produce frozen all-purpose features that rival text-supervised ones.
contributions: An automatic pipeline that builds the curated LVD-142M dataset by retrieval from an uncurated pool, with no metadata or text
A stabilised and faster discriminative SSL recipe (DINO + iBOT + SwAV centering + KoLeo + high-resolution phase), about 2x faster and 1/3 memory vs iBOT
Distillation of ViT-g/14 into smaller ViT-S/B/L models
Release of models and code, evaluation on image, video, retrieval, segmentation and depth, plus fairness and carbon analysis

method.summary: A ViT-g/14 (1.1B params) is trained from scratch on 142M curated images with a combined DINO image-level and iBOT patch-level self-distillation loss, untied heads, Sinkhorn-Knopp centering, KoLeo regulariser and a short 518x518 phase. Smaller ViT-S/B/L are distilled from the ViT-g. Features are evaluated frozen with linear probes, kNN, retrieval and light decoders.
method.task: self-supervised visual representation pretraining; frozen-feature evaluation

datasets.name: LVD-142M
datasets.source: retrieved from an uncurated pool of crawled web images (1.2B unique in Sec 3, 1.3B in App A.3; 744M after self- and relative deduplication) using ViT-H/16 SSL embeddings and cosine similarity to curated sets (ImageNet-22k, ImageNet-1k train, Google Landmarks v2, fine-grained sets, Table 15)
datasets.preprocessing: PCA hash dedup, NSFW filtering, face blurring; copy-detection dedup (k=64 neighbours, similarity >0.6; relative dedup against eval sets >0.45); retrieval N=4 neighbours (k=4 for GLDv2/IN-22k, k=32 for IN-1k) or cluster-based with 100,000 k-means clusters, 10,000 images per cluster, max 1M per dataset

datasets.name: ImageNet-22k
datasets.source: used as an ablation baseline and part of LVD curated set

datasets.name: ImageNet-1k
datasets.split: val for linear/kNN; ReaL and V2 also

datasets.name: Oxford/Paris (Revisiting), Met, AmsterTime
datasets.size: Oxford base 4,993; Paris base 6,322; Met train 397,121; AmsterTime 1,231 new+old
datasets.source: Table 15 and 18; their train/base splits are also used as retrieval queries when building LVD-142M

datasets.name: ADE20K, Cityscapes, VOC 2012, NYUd, KITTI, SUN RGB-D, iNaturalist 2018/2021, Places205, UCF101, K400, SSv2, Dollar Street, Casual Conversations
datasets.source: Table 18 lists use as pretraining-retrieval and eval

models.name: DINOv2 ViT-g/14
models.architecture: ViT, SwiGLU FFN, embed 1536, 24 heads (64 dim/head), 40 blocks

models.name: DINOv2 ViT-L/14 (distilled)
models.architecture: ViT, MLP FFN, embed 1024, 16 heads, 24 blocks

models.name: DINOv2 ViT-B/14 (distilled)
models.architecture: ViT, MLP FFN, embed 768, 12 heads, 18 blocks

other.note: Table 17 prints 18 blocks for ViT-B, 12 for heads

models.name: DINOv2 ViT-S/14 (distilled)
models.architecture: ViT, MLP FFN, embed 384, 6 heads, 12 blocks

other.also: OpenCLIP ViT-H/14, CLIP ViT-L/14, SWAG ViT-H/14, EVA-CLIP ViT-g/14

models.name: SSL baselines: MAE ViT-H/14, DINO ViT-B/8, SEERv2, MSN, EsViT, Mugs, iBOT ViT-L/16

training.objective: DINO image-level cross-entropy on class token + iBOT masked patch-level cross-entropy + KoLeo (weight 0.1) ; separate (untied) heads; Sinkhorn-Knopp centering (3 iterations) for teacher
training.lr_schedule: cosine weight-decay schedule 0.04 to 0.2; teacher momentum cosine 0.994 to 1; high-res phase reduces base lr
training.steps: 625k iterations; plus 10k iterations of high-resolution adaptation at 518x518
training.seq_len: inferred: 224 global crops and 98 local crops at patch 14
training.precision: float16 (DINO head gradients reduced in float32); FSDP with float32 weight shards
training.regularisation: stochastic depth 0.4 (from scratch), LayerScale init 1e-5, KoLeo, none for distilled models
training.hardware: A100 GPUs, PyTorch 2.0, FSDP; data pipeline on 20 nodes of 8 V100-32GB
training.compute: 22,016 A100-40GB GPU-hours for ViT-g (9.7 MWh, 3.7 tCO2eq)

other.ablation_recipe: Table 1 on ViT-L / ImageNet-22k adds one component at a time, k-NN 72.9 to 82.0
other.distillation: frozen ViT-g teacher, EMA of student as final model, no masking, no stochastic depth, iBOT loss on the two global crops
other.teacher_ema: teacher initialised from student, updated each step
other.ViT-g_arch_note: 1536 dim / 24 heads rather than 1408 / 16 of Zhai et al. 2022 for efficiency

inference.samples: single run per model; no seeds or variance reported
inference.retrieval: image retrieval evaluated by cosine similarity ranking of frozen features

other.linear_probe: SGD, 12500 iterations, random-resized-crop; grid over lr {0.0001..0.5}, output layers {1,4}, concatenating avg-pooled patch tokens {yes,no}; best validation accuracy reported
other.segmentation: linear layer on patch tokens upsampled to 512x512; +ms: last 4 layers, resolution 640, multiscale test-time augmentation
other.depth: lin.1, lin.4 (layers 3,6,9,12 for S/B; 5,12,18,24 for L; 10,20,30,40 for g), DPT decoder; 256 bins
other.video: 8 evenly spaced frames, average features (concat for SSv2)

metrics.name: Top-1 accuracy
metrics.definition: linear probe or kNN on frozen features, ImageNet-1k val

metrics.name: mAP
metrics.definition: mean average precision of cosine-similarity ranking, Oxford/Paris/AmsterTime

eval.protocol: Frozen backbone with simple heads; authors re-run all baselines with their own code and report the best of a lr/layers grid on the validation set itself; single run, no significance tests; for non-ImageNet tables only the four best SSL baselines and OpenCLIP-G are shown

availability.data: LVD-142M pipeline described; the 142M set itself not stated as released

evidence.quote: All models run for 625k iterations with optimizer AdamW

results.claim: DINOv2 ViT-g/14 frozen-feature linear probe on ImageNet-1k slightly exceeds OpenCLIP ViT-G/14.
results.setup: ImageNet-1k val, linear probe on frozen features, 224x224, all models evaluated with the authors' own code; DINOv2 ViT-g/14 (LVD-142M, no text) vs OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 (LAION-2B, text-supervised)
results.note: Text says the gap is +0.3%; EVA-CLIP ViT-g/14 is 86.4 (+0.1).
results.table: Table 4, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column linear val; baseline row OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 = 86.2

results.claim: On Oxford-Hard instance retrieval, DINOv2 ViT-L/14 scores 54.0 mAP against 19.7 for OpenCLIP ViT-G/14; the ViT-g/14 scores 52.3, so 54.0 is the ViT-L, not the largest model.
results.setup: Revisiting Oxford Hard, non-parametric cosine-similarity ranking of frozen features; DINOv2 ViT-L/14 vs OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 (19.7). Oxford 'base' images were a query set for building LVD-142M
results.note: DINOv2 ViT-g/14 gets 52.3 on Oxford-H (gain 32.6 over OpenCLIP); the text's '+34% mAP on Oxford-Hard' matches the ViT-L number (54.0-19.7=34.3).
results.table: Table 9, row DINOv2 ViT-L/14, column Oxford H; baseline row OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 column H = 19.7

results.claim: Instance-retrieval gap over weakly-supervised features is reported as +34 mAP on Oxford-Hard (+41 over SSL).
results.setup: Table 9, best DINOv2 vs OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 / best SSL baseline
results.quote: our features significantly outperform both SSL (+41% mAP on Oxford-Hard), and weakly-supervised (+34% mAP on Oxford-Hard) ones

results.claim: DINOv2 ViT-g/14 is far above OpenCLIP on Oxford-M, Paris-H and AmsterTime but not on every retrieval column.
results.setup: Table 9 ViT-g/14 row (Oxford M, Paris M, Paris H, AmsterTime mAP); OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 gets 50.7, 79.2, 60.2, 24.6
results.table: Table 9, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, columns Oxford M, Paris M, Paris H, AmsterTime mAP

results.claim: On the Met artwork benchmark OpenCLIP is far behind SSL baselines, and DINOv2 ViT-g/14 GAP is 36.8.
results.setup: Met, Table 9, DINOv2 ViT-g/14 vs OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 (6.5)
results.note: ViT-L/14 is higher (40.0); GAP- of ViT-g is 73.6.
results.table: Table 9, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column GAP

results.claim: The new components lift ImageNet-1k linear accuracy by 4.2 points over the previous SSL state of the art (iBOT ViT-L/16 on ImageNet-22k).
results.setup: ImageNet-1k linear probe, frozen features, DINOv2 ViT-g/14 vs iBOT ViT-L/16 INet-22k
results.quote: very significant improvement (+4.2%) over the previous state of the art (iBOT ViT-L/16 trained on ImageNet-22k) on linear evaluation

results.claim: Linear-probe robustness: DINOv2 ViT-g/14 beats OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 on ImageNet-A but trails on R and Sketch.
results.setup: ImageNet-A, linear classifier trained on ImageNet-1k, 224; OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 = 63.8
results.note: Im-R 78.8 vs 87.8; Sketch 62.5 vs 66.4; Im-C (lower better) 28.2 vs 45.3.
results.table: Table 6, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column Im-A

results.claim: Frozen ViT-g/14 on iNaturalist 2018 and 2021 beats OpenCLIP by wide margins and lags slightly on Places205.
results.setup: iNaturalist 2018, linear probe with augmentation, OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 = 73.0
results.note: Text: +8.6 and +9.7 for iNat2018/2021, -2.3 on Places205.
results.table: Table 7, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column iNat2018

results.claim: Averaged over 12 fine-grained benchmarks DINOv2 ViT-g/14 beats OpenCLIP ViT-G/14.
results.setup: 12 SimCLR transfer classification benchmarks, logistic regression on precomputed features
results.table: Table 8, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column Avg; OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 = 91.9

results.claim: Frozen ADE20K linear segmentation: DINOv2 ViT-g/14 reaches 49.0 mIoU vs 39.3 for OpenCLIP ViT-G/14.
results.setup: ADE20K, linear layer on patch tokens, upsampled to 512x512
results.table: Table 10, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column ADE20k lin.

results.claim: Frozen ViT-g/14 backbone with ViT-Adapter and Mask2Former head reaches 60.2 mIoU on ADE20K, close to the 62.9 state of the art.
results.setup: ADE20K; adapter and head trained, backbone frozen (66% of weights frozen); segmentation training took 28 hours on 16 V100 GPUs
results.quote: we reach 60.2 mIoU on ADE20k, close to the competitive state of the art, standing at 62.9 mIoU

results.claim: Depth estimation on NYUd with a DPT decoder over frozen ViT-g/14 gives RMSE 0.279 versus 0.414 for OpenCLIP ViT-G/14.
results.setup: NYUd, frozen backbone, DPT decoder
results.table: Table 11, row DINOv2 ViT-g/14, column NYUd DPT

results.claim: Training on curated LVD-142M beats uncurated data and ImageNet-22k on most benchmarks (except ImageNet-1k vs INet-22k).
results.setup: ViT-g/14, same number of iterations, shorter than final run, no high-res adaptation; Oxford-M column; uncurated 54.3, INet-22k 62.5
results.note: iNat2018: LVD 82.3 vs uncurated 68.0 vs INet-22k 81.1; INet-1k: LVD 85.8 vs INet-22k 85.9.

results.setup: Table 3a, Oxford-M: 55.6 without KoLeo, 63.9 with

results.setup: Table 3b, ADE-20k: 44.2 without MIM, 47.1 with

results.setup: Fig 5; scratch ViT-L/14 = 84.5, teacher ViT-g/14 = 86.5

results.setup: ViT-L/16 on ImageNet-1k, 224 vs 416 from scratch
results.quote: training at 416 is approximately 3 × more compute-intensive than training at 224

results.setup: same hardware vs iBOT code
results.quote: the DINOv2 code runs around 2× faster using only 1/3 of the memory

results.claim: Reproducing the DINOv2 ViT-g costs 22,016 A100-40GB GPU-hours, 9.7 MWh and 3.7 tCO2eq.
results.setup: A100-40GB at 400W, PUE 1.1, 0.385 kg CO2e/kWh; OpenCLIP ViT-L / ViT-G would need 22.4 / 118.9 MWh (text-encoder included)

results.setup: Dollar Street (16,073 images, 289 households, 54 countries, 94 concepts)
results.quote: our model performance drops by 25.7% compared to Europe

results.claim: The full project footprint is estimated at 0.5k to 1k tCO2eq, about 200k GPU-days.
results.setup: whole project, same grid assumptions

results.claim: LVD-142M is 142,109,386 images built in under two days on 20 nodes of 8 V100-32GB.
results.setup: retrieval from an uncurated pool deduplicated to 744M images
results.note: Pool size is printed as 1.2B (Sec 3) and 1.3B (App A.3), 1.1B after self-dedup, 744M after relative dedup.

limits: No variance, seeds or significance tests; single runs.
Linear-probe hyperparameters are picked on the validation set used for reporting, and the authors note SSL methods were developed using ImageNet-1k val as a debugging signal.

Many evaluation datasets (Oxford, Paris, Met, AmsterTime, ImageNet-1k, ADE20k, etc.) also supply train images as queries to build LVD-142M (Table 18, Table 15), so the data is tuned to those domains; near-duplicates of eval sets are removed.
Fairness: significant bias toward wealthy Western households remains (Africa -25.7% vs Europe; low vs high income -31.7%); authors say a more thorough bias evaluation may reveal flaws.
Comparison with OpenCLIP is on frozen features and linear heads; OpenCLIP trains a text encoder too, so the carbon comparison is acknowledged as unfair.
Training time, epochs and wall clock are not stated; epochs null.

terms.definition: Curated 142M-image pretraining dataset assembled by retrieving uncurated images close to curated sets
Kozachenko-Leonenko entropy estimator based loss that encourages uniform span of features within a batch
concatenate crops of different lengths into one sequence with a block-diagonal attention mask
